html:
SMTO-CMP-0045 — SMTO can't finish the task while other steps are still running

GUID: d867ea65-d5d8-4bb0-8df7-8bc1f454c682
Slug: completion-foreground-activities-pending
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The task tried to finish while other steps running alongside it were still in progress or waiting to start. The answer so far and any finished results are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look through the steps listed under this task for any that still show as running or waiting. SMTO runs some steps side by side and must wait for all of them before it can finish.
  2. Let the task keep running. It normally finishes by itself once those steps end. This block clears as soon as the last step running alongside the others has ended.
  3. If a step looks stuck and you no longer need it, select the Stop button beside that step, or Stop on the task. Stopping does not undo anything already done. Stopping ends the unfinished steps so the task no longer waits on them.
  4. Before asking SMTO to repeat any step, open it and read its output to check whether it already ran. Running a step again could repeat a change that already happened.

What success looks like

  • No steps under the task show as running, and the task shows Completed with its answer.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking again. Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the request to force the task to finish; some steps may already have made their changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion validation blocked the task's finish because another foreground-batch activity is still pending, runnable or running, or an accepted deferred wait is still outstanding.

What this means

  • Foreground-batch validation finds another activity pending, runnable or running, excluding the currently completing activity. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Foreground-batch validation finds another activity pending, runnable or running, excluding the currently completing activity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact sibling activity identities and current results.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the activity_ids or operation_ids listed in the requirements against the run's foreground_batch activities and outstanding deferred waits. Let them settle or cancel them through the task's Stop control before completion is declared again; do not launch duplicate operations to satisfy the check.
  • Wait for the current foreground activities to settle and inspect their results before completing the task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect existing activities and their effects. Do not launch duplicate work to make the completion check pass.

How to verify the fix

  • Required foreground siblings settle before the task makes its terminal claim.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
